name: Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector
storyHook: Humans left me behind in the dust of Tranquility Base in 1969. I have no batteries, no computer chips, and no moving parts. Yet every week, scientists on Earth shoot super-powered green lasers across 238,000 miles of space directly at my face.
scienceBreakthrough: Proved the Moon is drifting away from Earth at a rate of 3.8 cm per year.

spaceMath.label: Laser Round-Trip
spaceMath.detail: Light speed to Moon and back

quiz.question: How long does it take for a laser shot from Earth to bounce off the Retroreflector and return?
quiz.explanation: Light travels at 186,000 miles per second! Round-trip to the Moon takes ~2.5 seconds.

name: Surveyor 3
storyHook: I thought I was going to be alone forever in the dark freezing nights of the Ocean of Storms. But 31 months after I landed, I heard footsteps!
scienceBreakthrough: First robotic lander visited by humans on another world; proved Earth bacteria could survive 2.5 years in lunar vacuum.

quiz.question: Which Apollo mission visited Surveyor 3 on the Moon in November 1969?
quiz.explanation: Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean landed within walking distance of Surveyor 3!

name: Opportunity Rover (Oppy)
storyHook: They gave me a 90-day warranty. I stayed alive for nearly 15 Earth years! I climbed steep mountain rims, survived freezing Martian winters, and rolled 28 miles across red dust.
scienceBreakthrough: Discovered hematite 'blueberries' proving liquid water once flowed across Mars.

quiz.question: How long was Opportunity originally planned to operate on Mars?
quiz.explanation: Opportunity was designed for a 90-day mission but astounded NASA by working for nearly 15 years!

name: InSight Lander
storyHook: While other rovers looked at the surface, I put my ear to the ground and listened to the heartbeat of Mars! I placed a delicate glass dome seismometer directly onto the red soil.
scienceBreakthrough: Recorded over 1,300 Marsquakes to map the internal crust, mantle, and core of Mars.

spaceMath.label: Power Drop
spaceMath.detail: Solar power reduced by dust layers

quiz.question: What instrument did InSight use to record over 1,300 Marsquakes?
quiz.explanation: InSight placed the SEIS seismometer on the Martian surface to record internal tremors.

name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
storyHook: Everyone said flying on Mars was impossible because the air is 100 times thinner than Earth's! But I spun my dual carbon-fiber blades at 2,400 RPMs and lifted off.
scienceBreakthrough: First powered, controlled flight on another planet; proved aerial scouting on Mars is viable.

quiz.question: Why is flying a helicopter on Mars much harder than flying on Earth?
options: Martian air is 100x thinner than Earth's
quiz.explanation: Mars has an extremely thin atmosphere (less than 1% of Earth's density), requiring high blade speeds to generate lift!

name: Voyager 1
storyHook: I am the farthest human traveler in history. I launched in 1977, flew past Jupiter and Saturn, and in 2012, I broke through the magnetic bubble of our Sun into interstellar space!
scienceBreakthrough: First human-made object to exit the heliosphere and record raw interstellar particles.

spaceMath.label: Signal Lag
spaceMath.detail: One-way light transit time to Earth

quiz.question: What famous golden item is attached to Voyager 1 to communicate with potential extraterrestrial life?
quiz.explanation: Voyager 1 carries a phonograph record containing sounds, music, and images from Earth!
